newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr steadies, support proving solid.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr steadies, support proving solid.

text.p: The Australian dollar continued its stabilisation after its sharp fall in response to Friday's surprise interest rate cut, with support below US$0.7650 proving solid through the morning.

While eroded rate differentials were a negative, firmer commodity prices were proving supportive. As well, regional trade was quietened by U.K. and U.S. market holidays today and a focus on the mark, which was rising after the French elections.
By noon (0200 GMT), the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7651/56, just above the US$0.7640/50 support zone, after opening at US$0.7663/68 and a Friday close of US$0.7680/85.

But while the dollar had steadied, there was still a significant near term downside risk. If it breached US$0.7640 it was expected to move quickly towards US$0.7600, as large stop loss orders were belived to be placed there, traders said.
However, the fact that offshore investors did not aggressively sell the dollar on Friday, and in fact were buyers at the lower levels, had provided support to the local market.
Commodity prices and some shortcovering after Friday's fall which saw the unit drop a full cent on news of the rate cut were also giving the local dollar a floor, traders said.

Australian cash rates, at 5.50 percent, are now level with the U.S. Fed Funds rate, which is expected to rise in 1997. Also, while another local cut cannot not be ruled out, rates in other countries, including Japan, were seen to have an upwards bias.

"What it means that the Australian dollar has lost, or is losing, it's high yield tag," UBS Australia chief economist Steve Roberts said. "That's one factor which suggests it may be under some downward pressure. Countering that is that commodity prices appear to be fairly consolidative at the moment, at better levels than we've seen for some time."

On the crosses, the Australian dollar was also easier, one of many currencies losing ground against the mark. The better than expected performance of the leftist parties in the French election led to buying of the mark on speculation that it may endanger the timtetable for European Union.
By noon, the dollar stood at 88.52/62 yen and 1.2848/59 marks, down on openings of 89.00/10 and 1.2893/05 and Friday closes of 88.89/99 yen and 1.2987/3000 marks.
In trade weighted terms the dollar was at 58.1, down from an opening 58.3 and a Friday close of 58.4.
